Failures: all: ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'onnxscript'; decoder_joint: ValueError: `fuse_loss_wer` is set, therefore encoder and target lengths must be provided as well!. list_export_subnets()=['encoder', 'decoder_joint'] and all attributes are resolvable, so the RNNT path is reachable in principle, but NeMo's Exportable.export cannot build it here because it calls torch.onnx.export without dynamo=False and torch 2.14's dynamo=True path needs the missing onnxscript package. The single-graph CTC export is unaffected and is what ships. Subnet(s) ['decoder_joint'] still fail on their own: this checkpoint's joint has fuse_loss_wer enabled, and that wrapper requires encoder_lengths in addition to the five inputs RNNTDecoderJoint.input_types documents (encoder_outputs, targets, target_length, input_states_1, input_states_2). Tracing it would need fuse_loss_wer disabled in the checkpoint config, i.e. a change to the model, which is out of scope here. The standalone encoder graph did export.

notes: Latency is the median of the timed runs and covers feature extraction + ONNX forward + CTC greedy decode. Model/session load time is measured separately and is NOT included.
RTF = latency / audio duration. Values below 1.0 are faster than realtime.
The .nemo reference uses the identical features, encoder, ctc_decoder and ctc_decoding modules as the ONNX graph, so latency and text are directly comparable.
CER/WER here are parity metrics against the .nemo CTC output, NOT accuracy against a human transcript. No ground-truth transcripts exist in this workspace, so no accuracy claim is made.
The ONNX graph outputs log-probabilities for all 22 languages at once (5633 classes); the decoder selects the target language's columns plus the blank column.
Export used model.cur_decoder='ctc' so the whole encoder+CTC head becomes ONE onnx graph.

NeMo's own model.export() was tried first and failed with ModuleNotFoundError: onnxscript, because torch 2.14's torch.onnx.export defaults to dynamo=True. The graph was therefore exported with dynamo=False, which is the same TorchScript exporter NeMo calls, using NeMo's input/output names and dynamic axes.

INT8 qualifies only if it decodes like FP32 on every real validation clip (mean CER <= 0.05, worst clip CER <= 0.40, mean argmax frame agreement >= 50%) AND the artifact is smaller than FP32. Several recipes usually qualify; --int8-prefer picks between them. A rejected INT8 is deleted rather than shipped.
No accuracy improvement is claimed: the only reference available is the .nemo CTC output itself.
